Sample type: Combined nose and throat swab (viral PCR)
Sample collected: 10:36 on 11/03/2020
Sample received in laboratory: 11:20 on 11/03/2020
Reported: 21:50 on 11/03/2020

Test: SARS-CoV-2 RNA by real-time RT-PCR
Result: POSITIVE

Comment: Detected. Clinical correlation advised. Patient noted to have hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air) at 06:52 on 11/03/2020 and was admitted to hospital at 12:21 on 11/03/2020 with a background of fever, cough and breathlessness. Result telephoned to the admitting medical team on authorisation. Infection control precautions to continue as per Trust COVID-19 isolation pathway. Please repeat swab if clinical suspicion persists despite this result or if the clinical picture changes."}, {"doc_id": "P1:ed_clerking", "text": "ED Clerking – 11/03/2020, 13:46

Presenting complaint: Five-day history of fever, dry cough and increasing breathlessness in a woman in her 60s-70s.

History: Worsening dyspnoea on exertion, subjective fevers and non-productive cough. No chest pain. No known COVID-19 contact reported. Background of hypertension. Independent at baseline, lives with family.

Observations: Temperature 38.1°C, HR 104 bpm, RR 26/min, BP 132/78 mmHg, SpO2 89% on air recorded at 06:52 on 11/03/2020, subsequently improved to 94% on 2L nasal cannula. NEWS2 score 6.

Examination: Tachypnoeic at rest, bilateral fine crackles at both lung bases, no wheeze. Cardiovascular and abdominal examination unremarkable. Alert and orientated.

Swab taken for SARS-CoV-2 PCR given clinical suspicion of COVID-19; sample sent to virology.

Impression: Suspected COVID-19 pneumonia with hypoxaemia.

Plan: Admit under medicine for oxygen therapy, monitoring and further investigation including chest X-ray and bloods (FBC, U&E, CRP, D-dimer). VTE risk assessment completed – high risk, enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis to be prescribed once weight and renal function confirmed. Patient initially declined admission and wished to go home; agreed to stay after discussion with family. Admitted to hospital at 12:21 on 11/03/2020. Isolation precautions in side room as per COVID-19 pathway. Repeat observations 4-hourly, escalate if deteriorating."}, {"doc_id": "P1:ward_round", "text": "Ward Round – 13/03/2020, day 3 of admission

Background: Admitted to hospital at 12:21 on 11/03/2020 with suspected COVID-19 pneumonia and hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air at 06:52 on 11/03/2020). SARS-CoV-2 PCR confirmed positive, reported 21:50 on 11/03/2020.

Observations today: Temperature 37.4°C, HR 92 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 95% on 2L nasal cannula, BP 128/76 mmHg. NEWS2 3, improving trend.

Bloods: CRP falling (from 148 to 96 mg/L), lymphocytes 0.9 x10^9/L, renal function normal, D-dimer mildly elevated.

VTE prophylaxis: Enoxaparin out of stock on the ward; first dose given once pharmacy delivered supply the next day. First dose given 07:38 on 13/03/2020. No bleeding risk identified; mechanical prophylaxis with TEDs used in the interim.

Escalation status: For ward-based care; full escalation discussed with patient and family, not for ICU at present given improving trajectory, for review if deteriorates.

Plan: Continue supportive care and oxygen weaning as tolerated. Daily bloods and observations. Continue enoxaparin od. Physiotherapy input for mobilisation. Review chest X-ray. Consider stepping down oxygen if SpO2 maintained >94% on air. Discuss discharge planning once stable off oxygen for 24 hours."}, {"doc_id": "P1:discharge_summary", "text": "Discharge Summary

Admission date/time: 12:21 on 11/03/2020
Discharge date/time: 21:57 on 01/04/2020

Diagnosis: COVID-19 pneumonitis, confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 10:36 on 11/03/2020, positive result reported 21:50 on 11/03/2020).

Presenting complaint: Fever, cough and breathlessness with hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air recorded 06:52 on 11/03/2020).

Hospital course: Admitted to the acute medical unit for oxygen therapy and monitoring. VTE thromboprophylaxis with enoxaparin was commenced, first dose given 07:38 on 13/03/2020 following a brief delay due to ward stock shortage. Oxygen requirement peaked at 4L via nasal cannula in the first week, with gradual improvement over the following two weeks. Remained on the ward throughout and did not require critical care input. Course complicated by prolonged fatigue and deconditioning requiring extended physiotherapy input prior to discharge. Inflammatory markers trended down; renal function remained normal throughout.

Medications on discharge: Enoxaparin continued for a further two weeks post-discharge for extended VTE prophylaxis given prolonged immobility. Regular paracetamol continued as required. Usual antihypertensive medication resumed unchanged.

Follow-up arrangements: Respiratory clinic review arranged within 2 weeks of discharge to assess recovery and consider need for further imaging.

GP actions: Please continue the extended enoxaparin course as prescribed and monitor for signs of bleeding. Please arrange follow-up bloods (FBC, U&E) one week after discharge and review medication compliance. Advise gradual return to activity and urgent review if breathlessness worsens."}, {"doc_id": "P1:clinic_letter", "text": "Respiratory Follow-up Clinic Letter

Dear Doctor,

Re: patient seen in clinic following recent admission with COVID-19 pneumonitis.

The patient was discharged from hospital at 21:57 on 01/04/2020 following an admission for COVID-19 pneumonia confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 10:36 on 11/03/2020, result reported 21:50 on 11/03/2020), complicated by hypoxaemia requiring supplemental oxygen during the admission. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis was given during admission, first dose 07:38 on 13/03/2020.

The patient was seen in follow-up clinic at 14:27 on 11/04/2020, approximately ten days after discharge.

Current symptoms: Ongoing mild exertional breathlessness and fatigue, improving compared with discharge. No cough, chest pain or haemoptysis. Sleeping and appetite improving. No calf swelling or symptoms to suggest venous thromboembolism.

Examination: SpO2 96% on air, RR 16/min, chest clear to auscultation bilaterally. No signs of respiratory distress.

Investigations: Chest X-ray performed in clinic showed resolving bibasal changes compared with admission imaging, no residual consolidation. Bloods showed normal inflammatory markers and renal function.

Plan: Reassured regarding good clinical and radiological recovery. Advised to continue gradual increase in activity. No further respiratory follow-up required unless symptoms recur, in which case would welcome re-referral. Extended enoxaparin course now complete; no further anticoagulation required.

Please continue to monitor recovery in primary care.

Yours sincerely,
Respiratory Medicine Team"}, {"doc_id": "P2:lab_report", "text": "Virology Report

Sample type: Combined nose and throat swab

Sample received: 17:55 on 05/03/2020

Test: SARS-CoV-2 RNA RT-PCR
Result: POSITIVE

Comment: Detected. Rapid turnaround given clinical urgency – patient hypoxaemic (SpO2 <92% on air) at 11:53 on 05/03/2020 and subsequently admitted to hospital at 20:22 on 05/03/2020. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis commenced 22:25 on 05/03/2020 as part of the admission bundle. Result communicated by telephone to the admitting SHO on authorisation. Continue droplet/contact precautions as per Trust COVID-19 isolation policy."}, {"doc_id": "P2:ed_clerking", "text": "ED Clerking – 05/03/2020, 21:22

Presenting complaint: Three-day history of fever, dry cough and shortness of breath in a woman in her 20s-30s.

History: No significant past medical history. Non-smoker. Reports worsening breathlessness over the previous 24 hours with mild pleuritic chest discomfort. No known asthma.

Observations: Temperature 38.4°C, HR 112 bpm, RR 28/min, BP 118/70 mmHg, SpO2 90% on air recorded at 11:53 on 05/03/2020, improved to 95% on 2L nasal cannula. NEWS2 score 7.

Swab taken for SARS-CoV-2 PCR at 17:12; result returned positive, reported 18:46 on 05/03/2020.

Examination: Tachypnoeic, reduced air entry at the right lung base with scattered crackles. Otherwise unremarkable examination.

Impression: Confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia with hypoxaemia, high NEWS2.

Plan: Admit for oxygen therapy and monitoring. Referral made to the medical SHO but no record of it being received; re-referred later in the shift. Admitted to hospital at 20:22 on 05/03/2020. VTE risk assessment: high risk, thromboprophylaxis to be prescribed on the ward. Chest X-ray and bloods including FBC, U&E, CRP, D-dimer, LFTs sent. Isolation in side room as per COVID-19 pathway. Escalation plan to be discussed with the medical team on arrival to the ward."}, {"doc_id": "P2:ward_round", "text": "Ward Round – 06/03/2020, 02:36 (overnight medical review, day 1 of admission)

Background: Admitted to hospital at 20:22 on 05/03/2020 with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia (SARS-CoV-2 PCR positive, reported 18:46 on 05/03/2020) and hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air at 11:53 on 05/03/2020).

Observations: Temperature 37.9°C, HR 108 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 94% on 2L nasal cannula, BP 122/72 mmHg. NEWS2 5.

Bloods: CRP 132 mg/L, lymphopenia noted, renal function normal, D-dimer elevated at 1.8 mg/L.

VTE prophylaxis: Enoxaparin first dose given 22:25 on 05/03/2020, tolerated well, no bleeding concerns. To continue once daily.

Escalation status: For full escalation including ITU if required given young age and reversible pathology; ceiling of care discussed and agreed as appropriate for critical care referral if deteriorates.

Plan: Continue supplemental oxygen, aim SpO2 >94%. Repeat bloods and chest X-ray in the morning. Continue enoxaparin od. Monitor NEWS2 hourly overnight given borderline score. Escalate to the medical registrar if RR >30 or increasing oxygen requirement. Encourage oral fluids and paracetamol for fever."}, {"doc_id": "P2:discharge_summary", "text": "Discharge Summary

Admission date/time: 20:22 on 05/03/2020
Discharge date/time: 16:03 on 22/03/2020

Diagnosis: COVID-19 pneumonia, confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 17:12 on 05/03/2020, positive result reported 18:46 on 05/03/2020).

Presenting complaint: Fever, cough and breathlessness with hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air at 11:53 on 05/03/2020).

Hospital course: Admitted to the acute medical unit requiring supplemental oxygen up to 4L via nasal cannula in the first week. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis commenced on admission, first dose given 22:25 on 05/03/2020, continued throughout admission without complication. Inflammatory markers peaked around day 3 then trended down steadily. Remained under ward-level care throughout; critical care review was discussed on admission but not required as clinical trajectory remained stable. Gradual improvement in oxygen requirement allowing weaning to air by day 12. Mobilised with physiotherapy input prior to discharge.

Medications on discharge: Enoxaparin course completed on the ward, not continued on discharge given resolution of immobility risk factors. Paracetamol as required for residual myalgia. No new regular medications started.

Follow-up arrangements: Respiratory clinic review arranged within 2 weeks of discharge to assess ongoing recovery.

GP actions: Please review general recovery at routine appointment, monitor for any new respiratory symptoms, and reinforce self-isolation guidance for household contacts as applicable."}, {"doc_id": "P3:lab_report", "text": "Virology Report

Comment: Detected. Patient had documented hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air) at 10:06 on 04/03/2020 and was admitted to hospital at 17:13 on 04/03/2020; enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis commenced 21:28 on 04/03/2020. Result telephoned to the on-call medical team on authorisation out of hours. Continue isolation precautions as per Trust COVID-19 pathway pending clinical review."}, {"doc_id": "P3:ed_clerking", "text": "ED Clerking – 04/03/2020, 18:44

Presenting complaint: Woman in her 20s-30s presenting with cough, fever and breathlessness, re-attending the same day.

History: Initially assessed earlier today with similar symptoms; declined admission at that time. Represents with worsening breathlessness and persistent fever. No significant past medical history, non-smoker.

Observations: Temperature 38.2°C, HR 106 bpm, RR 24/min, BP 116/68 mmHg, SpO2 91% on air recorded at 10:06 on 04/03/2020 at first attendance, now 90% on air on this attendance. NEWS2 6.

Examination: Mildly tachypnoeic, bilateral basal crackles on auscultation, no wheeze. Alert, no confusion.

Impression: Suspected viral pneumonia, likely COVID-19 given clinical picture and current outbreak; awaiting swab.

Plan: Declined admission on first assessment and re-presented later the same day for admission. Admit under medicine for oxygen therapy, monitoring and swab for SARS-CoV-2 PCR to be sent. Admitted to hospital at 17:13 on 04/03/2020. VTE risk assessment: high risk given acute illness and reduced mobility, thromboprophylaxis to be prescribed once admission bloods reviewed. Chest X-ray and routine bloods requested including FBC, CRP, U&E, D-dimer. Isolation in side room. Escalation plan and ceiling of care to be discussed with the medical team on the ward."}, {"doc_id": "P3:ward_round", "text": "Ward Round – 04/03/2020, 23:27 (evening medical review, day of admission)

Background: Admitted to hospital at 17:13 on 04/03/2020 with suspected COVID-19 pneumonia and documented hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air at 10:06 on 04/03/2020). Swab for SARS-CoV-2 PCR taken 21:56 on 04/03/2020, result awaited.

Observations: Temperature 37.8°C, HR 98 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 94% on 2L nasal cannula, BP 120/70 mmHg. NEWS2 4.

Bloods: CRP 88 mg/L, mild lymphopenia, renal function normal, D-dimer mildly raised.

VTE prophylaxis: Pharmacist confirmed the prescription was signed and the first dose was given on time. Enoxaparin first dose given 21:28 on 04/03/2020, no bleeding risk identified.

Escalation status: For full escalation including critical care referral if required given young age and reversible illness; discussed and agreed with the patient.

Plan: Continue oxygen therapy, aim SpO2 >94%. Repeat observations and bloods in the morning. Continue enoxaparin od. Chest X-ray review pending. Await swab result. Encourage fluids, paracetamol for fever, monitor NEWS2 4-hourly."}, {"doc_id": "P3:discharge_summary", "text": "Discharge Summary

Admission date/time: 17:13 on 04/03/2020
Discharge date/time: 02:41 on 22/03/2020

Diagnosis: COVID-19 pneumonia, confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 21:56 on 04/03/2020, positive result reported 23:53 on 04/03/2020).

Presenting complaint: Fever, cough and breathlessness with hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air recorded 10:06 on 04/03/2020).

Hospital course: Admitted to the acute medical unit for oxygen therapy and monitoring. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis commenced on admission, first dose given 21:28 on 04/03/2020, continued throughout without complication. Oxygen requirement peaked at 3L via nasal cannula during the first week with subsequent gradual improvement. Remained ward-based throughout and did not require critical care input, though this had initially been discussed given the severity of presentation. The prolonged admission reflected slow resolution of fatigue and oxygen requirement rather than any acute deterioration. Physiotherapy input provided for reconditioning prior to discharge.

Medications on discharge: Enoxaparin course completed during admission; not continued on discharge as mobility had returned to baseline. Paracetamol continued as required for residual myalgia.

Follow-up arrangements: Respiratory clinic review arranged within 2 weeks of discharge to assess recovery and consider further investigation if symptoms persist.

GP actions: Please monitor ongoing recovery, review for any residual breathlessness or fatigue, and advise gradual return to normal activity."}, {"doc_id": "P3:clinic_letter", "text": "Respiratory Follow-up Clinic Letter

Dear Doctor,

Re: patient seen in clinic following recent admission with COVID-19 pneumonia.

The patient was discharged from hospital at 02:41 on 22/03/2020 following an admission for COVID-19 pneumonia confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 21:56 on 04/03/2020, result reported 23:53 on 04/03/2020), complicated by hypoxaemia requiring supplemental oxygen during admission. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis was given during admission.

The patient was seen in follow-up clinic at 19:19 on 31/03/2020.

Current symptoms: Mild residual fatigue and occasional exertional breathlessness, both improving. No cough, chest pain, calf swelling or symptoms suggestive of venous thromboembolism.

Examination: SpO2 97% on air, RR 15/min, chest clear to auscultation bilaterally, no signs of respiratory distress.

Investigations: Chest X-ray in clinic showed near-complete resolution of previous basal changes. Bloods showed normal inflammatory markers and renal function.

Plan: Reassured regarding good clinical and radiological recovery. Advised to continue gradual return to normal activity, including work and exercise as tolerated. No further respiratory follow-up required unless symptoms recur, in which case would welcome re-referral.

Please continue to support recovery in primary care.

Yours sincerely,
Respiratory Medicine Team"}, {"doc_id": "P4:lab_report", "text": "Virology Report

Sample type: Combined nose and throat swab
Sample collected: 13:08 on 05/03/2020
Sample received: 14:05 on 05/03/2020
Reported: 20:40 on 05/03/2020

Test: SARS-CoV-2 RNA RT-PCR
Result: POSITIVE

Comment: Detected. Patient subsequently developed hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air) at 21:30 on 05/03/2020; treating team informed by telephone on authorisation of result. Continue isolation precautions as per Trust COVID-19 pathway and clinical correlation as required."}, {"doc_id": "P4:ed_clerking", "text": "ED Clerking – 06/03/2020, 01:11

Presenting complaint: Woman in her 20s-30s presenting with cough, fever and progressive breathlessness.

History: Four-day history of dry cough and fever, with breathlessness worsening over the previous 24 hours. No significant past medical history, non-smoker. Swab for SARS-CoV-2 PCR taken 13:08 on 05/03/2020 during initial assessment. Laboratory warned of a possible backlog but the result was reported within the day. Result confirmed positive, reported 20:40 on 05/03/2020.

Observations: Temperature 38.6°C, HR 118 bpm, RR 30/min, BP 110/64 mmHg, SpO2 dropped to 88% on air recorded at 21:30 on 05/03/2020, improved to 93% on 4L via nasal cannula. NEWS2 score 8.

Examination: Marked tachypnoea, widespread bilateral crackles, using accessory muscles. Alert, no confusion, peripherally warm.

Impression: Confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia with significant hypoxaemia and high NEWS2, concerning for deterioration.

Plan: Admit urgently for oxygen therapy and close monitoring. Bed initially unavailable on AMU; a side room was found and the patient transferred within the hour. Admitted to hospital at 00:11 on 06/03/2020. VTE risk assessment: high risk, thromboprophylaxis to be prescribed on the ward. Chest X-ray and bloods sent including FBC, CRP, U&E, D-dimer, ABG. Critical care outreach informed given high NEWS2 for early review. Escalation plan and ceiling of care to be discussed on the ward."}, {"doc_id": "P4:ward_round", "text": "Ward Round – 07/03/2020, 00:33 (overnight consultant review, intensive care unit)

Background: Admitted to hospital at 00:11 on 06/03/2020 with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia and hypoxaemia. Required rapid escalation and was admitted to the intensive care unit at 09:09 on 06/03/2020 for ongoing respiratory support.

Observations: Temperature 37.6°C, HR 96 bpm, RR 24/min, SpO2 95% on CPAP with FiO2 0.5, BP 118/70 mmHg. NEWS2 not routinely scored on organ support.

Bloods: CRP falling from peak, lymphopenia persisting, renal function stable, ABG showing mild residual hypoxaemia with normal pH and lactate.

VTE prophylaxis: Enoxaparin first dose given 10:00 on 06/03/2020, continued once daily, no bleeding concerns identified.

Escalation status: Full escalation of care in place, for continued organ support as required; discussed with family regarding progress.

Plan: Continue CPAP with aim to wean FiO2 as tolerated. Continue enoxaparin od. Daily bloods and ABG. Proning to be considered if oxygenation deteriorates. Physiotherapy and nursing care to continue. Review again on morning ward round with ICU team."}, {"doc_id": "P4:icu_note", "text": "ICU Admission Note

Reason for admission: Confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia with progressive hypoxaemia and increasing oxygen requirement on the ward. Admitted to hospital at 00:11 on 06/03/2020, transferred to the intensive care unit at 09:09 on 06/03/2020 for escalation of respiratory support. ICU capacity was tight but a bed was accepted without delay.

Respiratory support: Commenced on CPAP via tight-fitting mask, initial FiO2 0.6 with PEEP 8cmH2O. SpO2 improved from 89% to 95% following initiation. Respiratory rate settled from 32/min to 24/min after one hour of support.

Ventilation details: Non-invasive respiratory support only at present; no indication for invasive ventilation. Continuous pulse oximetry and regular arterial blood gas monitoring in place.

Organ support: No renal, cardiovascular or other organ support required at present. Cardiovascularly stable, no vasopressor requirement. Urine output satisfactory.

VTE prophylaxis: Enoxaparin first dose given 10:00 on 06/03/2020 as per critical care thromboprophylaxis protocol, no contraindication identified.

Plan: Continue CPAP with staged weaning of FiO2 as oxygenation allows. Repeat ABG in four hours. Daily bloods including inflammatory markers and renal function. Proning to be considered if oxygenation does not improve further. Discuss ceiling of care and escalation plan with family. Continue enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis and regular observations. Review by ICU consultant on morning round."}, {"doc_id": "P4:discharge_summary", "text": "Discharge Summary

Admission date/time: 00:11 on 06/03/2020
Discharge date/time: 19:29 on 15/03/2020

Diagnosis: COVID-19 pneumonia complicated by type 1 respiratory failure, confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 13:08 on 05/03/2020, positive result reported 20:40 on 05/03/2020).

Presenting complaint: Fever, cough and progressive breathlessness with hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air at 21:30 on 05/03/2020).

Hospital course: Admitted to the acute medical unit and rapidly escalated to the intensive care unit on 06/03/2020 for CPAP respiratory support due to increasing oxygen requirement. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis commenced during ICU admission, first dose given 10:00 on 06/03/2020. Did not require invasive ventilation or other organ support during the ICU stay. Oxygenation improved over several days allowing stepdown to the ward, with subsequent successful weaning from supplemental oxygen. Physiotherapy input supported recovery of exercise tolerance prior to discharge.

Medications on discharge: Enoxaparin course completed prior to discharge, not continued at home given return to full mobility. No new regular medications commenced.

Follow-up arrangements: Respiratory clinic review arranged within 2 weeks of discharge to assess ongoing respiratory recovery given the need for CPAP support during admission.

GP actions: Please monitor recovery of exercise tolerance, review for any persistent breathlessness, and support gradual return to usual activities. Advise re-presentation if symptoms of respiratory deterioration recur."}, {"doc_id": "P5:lab_report", "text": "Virology Report

Comment: Detected. Patient subsequently developed hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air) at 21:20 on 07/03/2020 and was admitted to hospital at 22:09 on 07/03/2020; enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis commenced 23:15 on 07/03/2020. Result telephoned to the admitting team on authorisation out of hours. Continue isolation precautions as per Trust COVID-19 pathway."}, {"doc_id": "P5:ed_clerking", "text": "ED Clerking – 08/03/2020, 00:42

Presenting complaint: Woman in her 60s-70s presenting with cough, fever and breathlessness.

History: Five-day history of dry cough and fever with worsening breathlessness over the preceding two days. Background of type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Lives independently, usually mobile without aids.

Observations: Temperature 38.3°C, HR 114 bpm, RR 28/min, BP 128/74 mmHg, SpO2 87% on air recorded at 21:20 on 07/03/2020, improved to 92% on 4L nasal cannula. NEWS2 score 8.

Swab for SARS-CoV-2 PCR taken 12:50 on 07/03/2020; result confirmed positive, reported 20:24 on 07/03/2020.

Examination: Tachypnoeic, bilateral widespread crackles, using accessory muscles. Alert and orientated, no confusion.

Impression: Confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia with severe hypoxaemia, high NEWS2, in a patient with relevant comorbidities.

Plan: Admit urgently for oxygen therapy and close monitoring. Admitted to hospital at 22:09 on 07/03/2020. VTE risk assessment: high risk, thromboprophylaxis prescribed; enoxaparin first dose given 23:15 on 07/03/2020. Chest X-ray and bloods sent including FBC, CRP, U&E, D-dimer, ABG. Critical care outreach informed given high NEWS2 for early review. Escalation plan and ceiling of care to be discussed with patient and family on the ward."}, {"doc_id": "P5:ward_round", "text": "Ward Round – 08/03/2020, 22:21 (consultant review, intensive care unit)

Background: Admitted to hospital at 22:09 on 07/03/2020 with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia and severe hypoxaemia. Deteriorated over the following day and was admitted to the intensive care unit at 18:07 on 08/03/2020 for escalation of respiratory support.

Observations: Temperature 38.0°C, HR 110 bpm, RR 28/min, SpO2 93% on CPAP with FiO2 0.6, BP 130/80 mmHg.

Bloods: CRP rising, lymphopenia present, renal function stable, ABG showing mild hypoxaemia with compensated respiratory acidosis.

VTE prophylaxis: Platelet count checked before prophylaxis and found to be normal; first dose given on schedule. Enoxaparin first dose given 23:15 on 07/03/2020, continued once daily.

Escalation status: Full escalation of care in place given reversible pathology; family updated on deterioration and current management.

Plan: Continue CPAP with close monitoring of oxygenation, consider proning if no improvement. Continue enoxaparin od. Daily bloods and ABG. Discuss ceiling of care and likelihood of invasive ventilation should further deterioration occur. Review with ICU consultant on next round."}, {"doc_id": "P5:icu_note", "text": "ICU Note – Day 7 of critical care admission

Reason for ongoing ICU care: Admitted to hospital at 22:09 on 07/03/2020 with confirmed COVID-19 pneumonia and severe hypoxaemia, admitted to the intensive care unit at 18:07 on 08/03/2020 for CPAP support. NEWS2 of 8 recorded but critical care review requested only after the consultant ward round. Patient remained on CPAP for several days with fluctuating oxygenation.

Overnight the patient developed worsening type 1 respiratory failure with increasing work of breathing and falling SpO2 despite maximal CPAP settings. Decision made to proceed to invasive ventilation. Intubation delayed as all ventilators were in use; equipment sourced from theatres. Invasive ventilation started at 04:29 on 15/03/2020, patient sedated and paralysed for intubation, tube position confirmed on chest X-ray.

Ventilation details: Lung-protective ventilation strategy, tidal volumes 6ml/kg predicted body weight, PEEP 10cmH2O, FiO2 0.7 post-intubation with improving oxygenation on repeat ABG.

Organ support: Noradrenaline commenced for haemodynamic support following sedation and positive pressure ventilation. Renal function stable, satisfactory urine output, no renal replacement therapy required at present.

VTE prophylaxis: Enoxaparin continued once daily since first dose at 23:15 on 07/03/2020, no bleeding concerns.

Plan: Continue lung-protective ventilation, wean FiO2 and PEEP as oxygenation allows. Consider proning given severity of hypoxaemia. Continue vasopressor support with target MAP >65mmHg. Daily bloods, ABG and chest X-ray. Discuss prognosis and plan candidly with family given severity of illness."}, {"doc_id": "P5:discharge_summary", "text": "Discharge Summary

Admission date/time: 22:09 on 07/03/2020
Discharge date/time: 11:22 on 15/03/2020

Diagnosis: COVID-19 pneumonia with type 1 respiratory failure, confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR (swab taken 12:50 on 07/03/2020, positive result reported 20:24 on 07/03/2020).

Presenting complaint: Fever, cough and progressive breathlessness with severe hypoxaemia (SpO2 <92% on air at 21:20 on 07/03/2020).

Hospital course: Admitted to the acute medical unit with rapid deterioration requiring escalation to the intensive care unit at 18:07 on 08/03/2020 for CPAP respiratory support. Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis commenced on admission, first dose given 23:15 on 07/03/2020, and continued throughout the critical care stay. Respiratory failure progressed despite maximal non-invasive support and invasive ventilation was commenced at 04:29 on 15/03/2020, with vasopressor support added for haemodynamic stability. The discharge date recorded in the electronic system is 11:22 on 15/03/2020; this summary is issued to document the critical care course to date and should be read alongside ICU nursing records, as the discharge timing appears discordant with the clinical course described above.

Medications: Enoxaparin thromboprophylaxis and other critical care medications to be reconciled against the current prescription chart by the receiving team.

Follow-up arrangements: Respiratory clinic review arranged within 2 weeks of discharge to assess recovery, subject to confirmation of clinical status.

GP actions: Please liaise with the hospital regarding current clinical status given the complexity of this admission and arrange follow-up as appropriate once further information is available."}]}
